item: The memory tier is re-resolved upward when the machine grows (R731)
refs: PR #2060; R731; field test 2026-11-14 row 60 (report 8.1 and 4.6)
summary: The budget was resolved once from the RAM total read at boot, so a Qubes VM whose balloon grew afterwards kept a small or medium tier for the whole session: the in-memory rollup off, or killed by a DuckDB limit sized for the smaller machine (five of eight field instances). The liveness thread now checks once a minute: a higher tier read on two checks at least 60 s apart re-resolves the budget, sized from the LOWER of the two readings. Upward only (a shrink never lowers the tier mid-run); growth inside one tier changes nothing; an operator's OO_DB_POOL_SIZE / OO_DB_MAX_OVERFLOW / OO_SQLITE_CACHE_MB still wins; OO_MEMORY_REGROW=0 keeps the boot budget. The connection pool and the per-connection page cache keep their boot sizes (a live engine cannot change the pool, and its LIFO boot connections keep their cache); the DuckDB limit and threads at the next rollup build (which snapshots its budget once, R147, and whose duckdb-limit hold is released by a larger limit), and whether the rollup runs at the next serve. Logged once per change with the old and new tier; resolved_reading() carries first_resolved_at and every change, and the session's high-water record is rewritten on a change, so a crash after it is read against the tier it ran under (the crash report names each change).
